By \(\textnormal{ass:bounded-entries}\), \(\textnormal{ass:strong-spectrum}\), and \(\textnormal{def:analytic-interval}\),
\[
|\theta_n|
\le\|u\|_2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2
\le (B\sqrt n){1\over cn}(B\sqrt n)
={B^2\over c}=M_0.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus the off-gate interval always covers \(\theta_n\).  On \(G_n\), condition on \(X\).  The established \(\textnormal{lem:conditional-reduction}\) gives
\[
Z_n=m_n+\xi_n,qquad \xi_n\mid X\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{2r}),
\qquad
\theta_{X,n}=\sigma^2m_{p,n}^{\top}D_nm_{q,n},
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{|\theta_{X,n}-\theta_n|>d_n,\,G_n\}
\le e^{-n/2}+3(e+n)^{-6}.
\tag{3}
\]
The gate gives \(s_r(X)>0\), so every diagonal entry of \(D_n\) is positive and \(D_n\) is invertible.  The established \(\textnormal{lem:gaussian-outer-inversion}\), applied conditionally to the realized \(D_n\) and \(m_n\), yields
\[
P\left\{|\widehat\theta_n-\theta_{X,n}|>\sigma^2W_n\mid X\right\}
\le\alpha
\quad\hbox{on \(G_n\)}.
\tag{4}
\]
If neither exceptional event in (3)--(4) occurs, the triangle inequality gives
\[
|\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n|
\le\sigma^2W_n+d_n,
\tag{5}
\]
so the on-gate interval covers.  Combining (1), (3), and the expectation of (4),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\theta_n\notin I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\}
\le\alpha+e^{-n/2}+3(e+n)^{-6}.
\tag{6}
\]
Taking the limit superior proves the asserted uniform coverage.  No step divides by \(\|u\|_2\), \(\|v\|_2\), or a target loading.

For the comparison clause, \(\textnormal{prop:yan-wainwright-class-embedding}\) proves, with the corrected normalization \(\omega=\sigma(n+1)\), that this is a square one-target subclass satisfying conditions \(4.1\)--\(4.4\mathrm b\) eventually.  The frozen \(\textnormal{lem:yan-wainwright-gaussian-condition}\) records that their Gaussian theorem additionally assumes condition \(4.4\mathrm c\), and the embedding proposition proves that this last condition fails at \(u=v=0\).  Equation (6) continues to hold there and along arbitrary approaches to joint zero.  The extension is therefore exactly the one asserted on the embedded subclass, with no claim about the rest of the published class.

Fix a sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) for which \(b_n/a_n\to0\).  In particular \(a_n>0\) eventually.  Write \(e_0=\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), \(U_0=\|u\|_2\), \(V_0=\|v\|_2\), and
\[
a_{X,n}:=\sigma^2s_D(m_n)
=\sigma\sqrt{\|uX_r^+\|_2^2+\|X_r^+v\|_2^2}.
\tag{1}
\]
We first compare (1) with \(a_n\).  On \(e_0\le cn/4\), the singular-vector equations give
\[
\|(I-UU^{\top})\widehat U\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\vee
\|(I-VV^{\top})\widehat V\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le {e_0\over cn-e_0}.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, for example,
\((I-UU^{\top})\widehat U\widehat S=(I-UU^{\top})E\widehat V\), and \(s_r(X)\ge cn-e_0\); the transpose equation is identical.  Put \(L=U^{\top}\widehat U\), \(M=V^{\top}\widehat V\), and \(B_X=U^{\top}X_rV=L\widehat S M^{\top}\).  Direct multiplication gives the sandwich identity
\[
V^{\top}X_r^+U=(MM^{\top})B_X^{-1}(LL^{\top}).
\tag{3}
\]
By (2), \(\|LL^{\top}-I\|_{\mathrm{op}}\vee\|MM^{\top}-I\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K e_0^2/n^2\).  Also
\(\|B_X-S\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2e_0\), and both \(B_X^{-1}\) and \(S^{-1}\) have norm at most \(K/n\).  The resolvent identity and (3) therefore yield
\[
\|V^{\top}X_r^+U-S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K{e_0\over n^2}.
\tag{4}
\]
The component of \(X_r^+U\) orthogonal to \(\operatorname{col}(V)\) is, by (2), at most \(Ke_0/n^2\); the transpose argument treats \(V^{\top}X_r^+-S^{-1}U^{\top}\).  Consequently
\[
\|(X_r^+-A^+)U\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|V^{\top}(X_r^+-A^+)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K{e_0\over n^2}.
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(v\in\operatorname{col}(U)\) and \(u^{\top}\in\operatorname{col}(V)\), the reverse triangle inequality applied to (1) and \(\textnormal{def:transition-scale}\) gives
\[
|a_{X,n}-a_n|
\le K\sigma{e_0\over n^2}(U_0+V_0).
\tag{6}
\]
Moreover, \(s_1(A)\le C_0n\) implies
\[
a_n\ge {\sigma(U_0+V_0)\over\sqrt2 C_0n}.
\tag{7}
\]
Thus \(|a_{X,n}/a_n-1|\le Ke_0/n\) on the displayed event.

For completeness, a \(1/4\)-net of the unit sphere has at most \(9^n\) points, by the disjoint-ball volume argument.  Applying the scalar Gaussian tail bound to two such nets gives constants \(K_1,k_1>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P_P(e_0>K_1\sqrt n+x)
\le2e^{-k_1x^2/\sigma^2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Hence \(e_0/n=o_P(1)\), \(P(G_n^c)\to0\), and (6)--(7) prove
\[
{a_{X,n}\over a_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{9}
\]
The singular-value perturbation inequality, obtained directly from the min--max formula, gives \(|s_j(X)-s_j(A)|\le e_0\).  Since \(r\le r_0\) and every nonzero singular value of \(A\) is at least \(cn\),
\[
{\sigma^2\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm F}\over b_n}
\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{10}
\]
Because \(h_n=\|D_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|D_n\|_{\mathrm F}\), (9)--(10) and \(b_n/a_n\to0\) imply
\[
{s_D(m_n)\over h_n}={a_{X,n}\over\sigma^2h_n}\longrightarrow\infty
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{11}
\]

The sequential assertion in \(\textnormal{lem:gaussian-outer-inversion}\) is uniform outside sufficiently large values of the ratio in (11): otherwise a countersequence would contradict that lemma.  Conditioning on \(X\), then using (11), gives, with \(z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\),
\[
{\sigma^2W_n\over z_\alpha a_{X,n}}\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability on \(G_n\)}.
\tag{12}
\]
The expectation conclusion of \(\textnormal{lem:conditional-reduction}\) and \(w_n/a_n=1+b_n/a_n\to1\) imply, by Markov's inequality,
\[
{d_n\mathbf1\{G_n\}\over a_n}\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{13}
\]
On \(G_n\), the length is \(2\sigma^2W_n+2d_n\); on \(G_n^c\), its value is irrelevant to convergence in probability because that event has probability tending to zero.  Equations (9), (12), and (13) prove
\[
{\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})
\over2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Only the divergence \(a_n/b_n\to\infty\) was used; no rate or loading pretest was imposed.

Let \(r=1\), and write the retained donor singular triplet as \((\widehat u,\widehat s,\widehat v)\).  By \(\textnormal{def:gaussian-coordinates}\) and \(\textnormal{def:analytic-halfwidth}\), the center is exactly
\[
\widehat\theta_n
=\sigma^2Z_{p,n}^{\top}D_nZ_{q,n}
={(R\widehat v)(\widehat u^{\top}C)\over\widehat s}
=RX_r^+C.
\tag{1}
\]
Its observed first-order scale is
\[
\widehat a_{X,n}:=\sigma^2s_{Z,n}
=\sigma\left\{{(\widehat u^{\top}C)^2+(R\widehat v)^2\over\widehat s^2}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{2}
\]
This is the rank-one plug-in version of the variance formula in Yan and Wainwright~\cite{YanWainwright2024}, equation \(4.5\mathrm b\).  Indeed, for the augmented mean in \(\textnormal{prop:yan-wainwright-class-embedding}\), write a compact SVD as \(\overline U\overline S\overline V^{\top}\), and let subscript \(1\) denote the first \(n\) rows.  Full column rank and the factorization of the donor block imply
\[
\overline U_{n+1,\boldsymbol\cdot}
(\overline U_1^{\top}\overline U_1)^{-1}\overline U_1^{\top}=uA^+,
\qquad
\overline V_1(\overline V_1^{\top}\overline V_1)^{-1}
\overline V_{n+1,\boldsymbol\cdot}^{\top}=A^+v.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(\omega^2/(NT)=\sigma^2\), their population first-order variance in the embedded problem is therefore exactly
\[
\gamma_{n+1,n+1}^{\star}
=\sigma^2\{\|uA^+\|_2^2+\|A^+v\|_2^2\}=a_n^2.
\tag{4}
\]
The corrected rates in the embedding proof allow the Yan--Wainwright tolerance to be chosen, for example, as a fixed multiple of \(\{\log(e+n)/n\}^{1/4}\) along \(b_n/a_n\to0\); their conditions and the additional sample-size inequality in Proposition~1 then hold eventually.  The cited \(\textnormal{lem:yan-wainwright-variance-consistency}\) and (4) consequently give
\[
{\sqrt{\widehat\gamma_{n+1,n+1}}\over a_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{4a}
\]

We next compare centers, rather than identifying two different algorithms by definition.  Let \(Z^{\mathrm{YW}}\) be the leading variable in the cited \(\textnormal{lem:yan-wainwright-master-decomposition}\).  Applying (3) and the corresponding full-factor formula for \(A^+\) to its three terms gives the exact identity
\[
Z^{\mathrm{YW}}=eA^+v+uA^+f+eA^+f.
\tag{5}
\]
Put \(U_0=\|u\|_2\) and \(V_0=\|v\|_2\).  Thus
\[
RX_r^+C-\theta_n-Z^{\mathrm{YW}}
=R(X_r^+-A^+)C.
\tag{6}
\]
The action bounds (5) in the proof of \(\textnormal{thm:oracle-length}\), their transpose, and the same singular-subspace calculation for the full operator give, on \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le cn/4\),
\[
\|X_r^+-A^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K{\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\over n^2}.
\tag{7}
\]
Expanding the right side of (6), using conditional Gaussian second moments for terms containing \(e\) or \(f\), (7), and \(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(\sqrt n)\), shows
\[
R(X_r^+-A^+)C=o_P(a_n)
\quad\hbox{whenever \(b_n/a_n\to0\)}.
\tag{8}
\]
For example, the two one-noise terms are
\(O_P\{(U_0+V_0)n^{-3/2}\}=o_P(a_n)\) by the lower bound (7) in the oracle-length proof, and the two-noise term is \(O_P(n^{-3/2})=o_P(a_n)\); the deterministic term is controlled by \(\textnormal{lem:conditional-reduction}\) and its allowance, which is \(o_P(a_n)\).

It remains to check the remainder in the published center.  Under the corrected normalization \(\omega=\sigma(n+1)\), the embedding proof gives \(\rho_{N,T}=O(n^{-1/2})\), target singular-row norms \(O(U_0/n)\) and \(O(V_0/n)\), and fixed sub-block conditioning.  Substitution into the four displayed quantities in the cited master decomposition gives
\[
\sum_{j=1}^4b_j(n+1,n+1)
\le K\left\{{(U_0+V_0)\sqrt{\log(e+n)}\over n^{3/2}}
+{U_0V_0\sqrt{\log(e+n)}\over n^2}
+{\log(e+n)\over n^{3/2}}\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Because \(U_0,V_0\le B\sqrt n\), the first two terms in (9) are \(o(a_n)\).  Also \(b_n/a_n\to0\), \(b_n\ge\sigma^2/(C_0n)\), and \(a_n\le K(U_0+V_0)/n\) imply \(U_0+V_0\to\infty\); hence the last term is also \(o(a_n)\).  The cited probability bound and (5)--(9) prove that the Yan--Wainwright center and (1) differ by \(o_P(a_n)\).

Finally, conditional on \(X\), \(Z_n=m_n+\xi_n\) and
\[
|s_{Z,n}-s_D(m_n)|\le h_n\|\xi_n\|_2.
\tag{10}
\]
The oracle-length proof gives \(a_{X,n}/a_n\to1\) and \(\sigma^2h_n/a_n=o_P(1)\).  Since \(r=1\) is fixed, (10) yields \(\widehat a_{X,n}/a_n\to1\).  The regular-limit part of \(\textnormal{lem:gaussian-outer-inversion}\) and \(d_n=o_P(a_n)\) then give
\[
\sigma^2W_n
=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\widehat a_{X,n}+o_P(a_n).
\tag{11}
\]
Equations (1), (4), (8)--(11) establish the claimed rank-one compatibility of both the center and first-order half-width.

Put \(\delta=2^{-p_n-1}\), let \(\mathcal B\) be the coordinate box of radius \(\delta\), and note that every public control has zero input radius under the proposed exact-dyadic premise.  We construct a coarse branch and a sharp branch.

Let \(T\) be a directed upper bound for every absolute coordinate on \(\mathcal B\), and at a trial working precision \(q\) set
\[
H=n+T+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q+1.
\]
At any point of the box at which \(G_n\) holds,
\[
\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le{2\over cn},
\qquad
\|Z_{p,n}\|_2\vee\|Z_{q,n}\|_2\le{\sqrt nT\over\sigma},
\qquad
t_{Z,n}\le{\sqrt{2n}T\over\sigma}=:\overline t.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover \(0<\zeta_\alpha(t)\le z_{\max}:=\Phi^{-1}(1-3\alpha/8)\).  Define
\[
\overline R=\sqrt{C_{r,\alpha}\log(e+2\overline t+A_{r,\alpha})}
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
\overline W={2\over cn}
\left\{z_{\max}(\overline t+\overline R)
+{C_{r,\alpha}\over2}\log(e+\overline t+\overline R)\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The definitions and monotonicity give \(W_n\le\overline W\).  Also
\[
|\widehat\theta_n|=|RX_r^+C|\le{2T^2\over c},
\tag{4}
\]
and
\[
d_n\le K_0\sigma^2\ell_n n^{-2}
\left({\sqrt nT\over\sigma}+\sqrt{\ell_n}\right)^2=:\overline d.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus every feasible on-gate interval is contained in
\[
[-\overline H,\overline H],
\qquad
\overline H={2T^2\over c}+\sigma^2\overline W+\overline d,
\tag{6}
\]
whereas every off-gate interval is \([-M_0,M_0]\).  Directed versions of (1)--(6) are computable without a spectral gap.  Replacing logarithms and square roots by the elementary majorants above shows that their magnitudes and exponent encodings are polynomial in the input bit lengths.  Hence the hull of (6) and the fallback is a certified coarse enclosure.

For the sharp branch use the invariant projectors
\[
P_R=\mathbf1_{((cn/2)^2,\infty)}(X^{\top}X),
\qquad
P_L=\mathbf1_{((cn/2)^2,\infty)}(XX^{\top}).
\tag{7}
\]
When the certified count above the threshold is \(r\),
\[
X_r=P_LXP_R,
\qquad
X_r^+=X_r^{\top}(X_rX_r^{\top}+I-P_L)^{-1}.
\tag{8}
\]
To verify (8), substitute a compact SVD \(X_r=U_rS_rV_r^{\top}\); the inverse is \(U_rS_r^{-2}U_r^{\top}+I-P_L\), and left multiplication by \(X_r^{\top}\) gives \(V_rS_r^{-1}U_r^{\top}\).

The proved proposed version of \(\textnormal{lem:certified-error-recurrence}\) supplies a polynomial-time inverse candidate for every inverse in the sign iteration and (8): after symmetrization it uses
\[
L_{k+1}=L_k(2I-\widehat K L_k),
\qquad L_0=\widehat K/\Lambda^2,
\tag{9}
\]
and the directly checked residual satisfies the solved recurrence \(r_{k+1}\le r_k^2+CH^d2^{-q}\).  Its proof shows that (9) reaches residual \(O(H^{d'}2^{-q})\) in \(O(\log H+\log(q+2))\) steps, with candidate norm at most \(2\|\widehat K^{-1}\|\).  For the sign iteration it also proves the noncommutative enclosure recurrence
\[
R_{j+1}\le{3\over2}R_j+CH^d2^{1-q}
\tag{10}
\]
and adds to the final projector radius the exact tail
\[
{\chi^{2^J}\over1-\chi^{2^J}}.
\tag{11}
\]
Equations (9)--(11) give both residual validity and polynomial bit complexity, rather than relying on an unspecified inverse oracle.  The exact endpoint depends only on
\[
RX_r^+C,quad
{1\over\sigma}\sqrt{\|X_r^+C\|_2^2+\|(X_r^+)^{\top}R^{\top}\|_2^2},quad
{\|P_RR^{\top}\|_2\over\sigma},quad
{\|P_LC\|_2\over\sigma}.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus rotations inside a repeated retained singular space change no endpoint.  A boundary tie is not accepted and invokes the coarse hull.

It remains to justify special functions and termination.  Repeated integration gives, for \(x\ge0\),
\[
F_{\chi^2_{2r}}(x)=1-e^{-x/2}\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}{(x/2)^j\over j!}.
\tag{13}
\]
Taylor's formula with its integral remainder gives
\[
\left|e^y-\sum_{j=0}^m{y^j\over j!}\right|
\le{e^{|y|}|y|^{m+1}\over(m+1)!},
\tag{14}
\]
and the Gaussian identity
\[
\Phi(x)={1\over2}+{1\over\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_0^xe^{-t^2/2}\,dt
\tag{15}
\]
has a directed rational evaluation of polynomial cost.  Explicitly, enclose \(\pi\) with Machin's identity
\[
\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)
\]
and the alternating series for \(\arctan\); \(O(s)\) terms give \(s\) certified bits.  Directed bisection then encloses \(\sqrt{2\pi}\).  On a bracket \(|x|\le X\), integrate the exponential Taylor polynomial termwise in (15); the remainder (14) shows that \(O(s+X^2+1)\) terms give \(s\) bits after binary range reduction.  All numerator and exponent lengths are polynomial in \(s\) and the bit length of \(X\).  The Chernoff calculation
\[
P(Z\ge x)\le\inf_{t>0}e^{-tx+t^2/2}=e^{-x^2/2}
\tag{16}
\]
provides a normal-quantile bracket of polynomial bit length, and (13) provides one of size \(O_{r_0}(1+\log(1/\gamma))\) at upper-tail probability \(\gamma\).  Because the densities are positive on finite interior brackets, directed probability-bracketed bisection returns an interval containing each quantile \(Q\) with width at most
\[
8\,2^{1-q}(1+|Q|).
\tag{17}
\]
Equations (13)--(17) use polynomially many operations in the requested precision, the input lengths, and \(\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\), since \(r\le r_0\) is fixed.

At successively doubled precisions up to
\[
q^\star=8\{n+L_n+p_n+\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil+1\}^2,
\tag{18}
\]
attempt the certified off-gate or common-split on-gate branch.  If neither succeeds, return the coarse hull.  There are \(O(\log q^\star)\) attempts.  Each attempt uses the explicit matrix iterations (9)--(11), polynomially many \(n\)-dimensional operations, and the scalar bisections above.  Mantissas and all stored exponent encodings have polynomial length.  This proves termination and polynomial bit complexity.

For a fixed \((X,R,C)\in\mathcal B\), write its exact interval as \([L,U]\) and the returned interval as \([\underline L,\overline U]\).  The recurrence induction, residual test, quantile brackets, and hull rule prove
\[
\underline L\le L\le U\le\overline U.
\tag{19}
\]
Endpointwise propagation gives
\[
0\le L-\underline L\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}},
\qquad
0\le\overline U-U\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}.
\tag{20}
\]
Adding (20) proves the length inequality.  Arbitrary-precision signed exponents exclude overflow and subnormals in the abstract model; the stated IEEE route emits no certificate unless rescaling and exponent widening exclude overflow, subnormal values, and flushing.  Finally, a supplied control interval can be inserted with half-width as input radius, but its production cost is not bounded without the additional uniform modulus stated in the proposed claim.  This proves the corrected certificate.

For \(x\ge0\), \(\sqrt x\le x+1\), and \(\log(e+n)\le n+1\); hence the displayed exact dyadic \(\overline\tau_n\) is at least \(\tau_n\).  The schedule and \(\textnormal{def:observation-encoding}\) give
\[
T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}
=2^{L_n-p_n-\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil-4}
=2^{\lceil\log_2\overline\tau_n\rceil+2g_n+C_\star-4}
\ge\overline\tau_n\ge\tau_n
\tag{1}
\]
when \(C_\star\ge4\).  The schedules \(p_n,q_n,L_n\), and the binary encoding length \(\lceil\log_2T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\rceil\), are polynomially bounded in \(n\) and \(\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\); numerically, \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) is bounded by a fixed power of \((n+2)/\alpha\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(L_n\) also dominates the fixed encoding lengths of the exact-dyadic public controls.  A rounded observation coordinate has numerator length at most
\[
p_n+\lceil\log_2(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)\rceil+2
\tag{2}
\]
and exponent-description length \(O(\log(p_n+2))\); a sufficiently large fixed \(C_\star\) therefore places every encoded input in \(\mathbb D_{L_n}\).

There are \(N_n=n^2+2n\le3n^2\) observed coordinates, each with mean bounded by \(B\).  For \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), exponential Markov inequalities give
\[
P(|Z|>x)\le2e^{-x^2/2},\qquad x\ge0.
\tag{3}
\]
By (1), a union bound yields
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P_P(\kappa_n=1)
\le2N_ne^{-6\log(e+n)}
\le6n^2(e+n)^{-6}=O(n^{-4})=o(n^{-1}).
\tag{4}
\]

We next control the only event on which the sharp numerical bound can fail.  Let \(\mathcal N\) be a \(1/4\)-net of the unit sphere with \(|\mathcal N|\le9^n\), obtained by the disjoint-ball volume comparison.  Approximation in both arguments gives
\[
\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_{x,y\in\mathcal N}|x^{\top}Ey|.
\tag{5}
\]
Each \(x^{\top}Ey/\sigma\) is standard normal.  Equations (3)--(5) imply constants \(k_0>0\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(c,\sigma\), for which
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P_P\{\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}>cn/8\}
\le2\,9^{2n}\exp\left(-{c^2n^2\over512\sigma^2}\right)
\le e^{-k_0n^2}
\tag{6}
\]
for \(n\ge n_0\).  The min--max formula gives
\[
|s_j(A+E)-s_j(A)|\le\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{7}
\]
On the complement of (6), exact rank and strong spectrum imply
\[
s_r(X)\ge7cn/8,\qquad s_{r+1}(X)\le cn/8,\qquad
s_1(X)\le C_0n+cn/8.
\tag{8}
\]
The true donor and any matrix in its encoding box differ entrywise by at most \(2^{-p_n}\), hence in operator norm by at most \(n2^{-p_n}\).  Since \(c\le1\) and \(C_0\ge2\), equations (8) imply, for all sufficiently large \(n\), that every matrix in the box satisfies
\[
s_r\ge3cn/4,\qquad s_{r+1}\le cn/4,\qquad
s_1\le3C_0n/2.
\tag{9}
\]

Put
\[
H_n=n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q_n+1.
\tag{10}
\]
The schedules make \(H_n\) a polynomial in \(n\) for fixed \(\alpha\).  The proposed and proved \(\textnormal{lem:stable-certified-padding}\), together with (6)--(9), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[&(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})
\mathbf1\{\kappa_n=0\}] 
&\le K H_n^k(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n})+K H_n^k e^{-k_0n^2}
=o(n^{-m})
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
for every fixed \(m>0\), because \(p_n=n^2+O(\log n)\) and \(q_n=n^2+O(\log n)\).  Every recorded radius is nonnegative and bounded by their sum, so (11) holds for each summand separately.  This also verifies the early-kill requirement uniformly for loading norms from zero through their \(B\sqrt n\) bound: the numerical estimate (11) does not divide by a loading.

The corrected \(\textnormal{thm:deterministic-dyadic-certificate}\) applies because all public controls are exact dyadics.  On \(\kappa_n=0\), it gives
\[
I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}},
\qquad
0\le\varepsilon_n
\le2(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})
=2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}}.
\tag{12}
\]
On \(\kappa_n=1\), the composed procedure returns \([-M_0,M_0]\).  This contains the target because
\[
|\theta_n|
\le\|u\|_2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2
\le(B\sqrt n){1\over cn}(B\sqrt n)=M_0.
\tag{13}
\]
Also \(0\le\varepsilon_n\le2M_0\) on that branch.  Equations (4), (11)--(13) prove
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]=o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[M_0\mathbf1\{\kappa_n=1\}]=o(n^{-1}),
\tag{14}
\]
as well as every summand-by-summand assertion.

Pointwise, (12)--(13) show that coverage by \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) entails coverage by \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\).  The proved \(\textnormal{thm:uniform-coverage}\) therefore gives the first limit.  Furthermore,
\[
w_n\ge b_n=\sigma^2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm F}
\ge{\sigma^2\over s_1(A)}\ge{\sigma^2\over C_0n}.
\tag{15}
\]
Combining (14)--(15),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}{\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]\over w_n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{16}
\]
Since \(x\le y+[x-y]_+\) for nonnegative \(x,y\),
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})
\le\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})+\varepsilon_n.
\tag{17}
\]
The established \(\textnormal{thm:transition-length}\) and (16) give the asserted transition-order expected length.

If \(b_n/a_n\to0\), equation (15) implies
\[
na_n\ge{\sigma^2\over C_0}{a_n\over b_n}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{18}
\]
By (14),
\[
{\mathbb E_{P_n}[\varepsilon_n]\over a_n}
={n\mathbb E_{P_n}[\varepsilon_n]\over na_n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{19}
\]
Thus \(\varepsilon_n/a_n\to0\) in \(L^1(P_n)\) and in probability.  On \(\kappa_n=0\), (12) makes the length difference nonnegative and at most \(\varepsilon_n\); the exceptional probability tends to zero by (4).  Therefore
\[
{\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})-
\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})\over a_n}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{20}
\]
The proved \(\textnormal{thm:oracle-length}\) and (20) establish the Gaussian length ratio.  Equations (11) and (14) are uniform over the entire class, so they imply the final rank-one joint-zero assertion as a special case.

Finally, suppose only one fixed dyadic interval of positive width is supplied for a public control that enters a strictly monotone quantile.  Two distinct control values in that interval induce two distinct quantiles.  An algorithm receiving the same fixed interval under both values cannot return enclosures of both with widths tending to zero.  Thus a nonrefinable interval is insufficient.  A refinement oracle avoids this indistinguishability only when its uniform production modulus is included in the schedules, exactly as stated.

Fix \(P=P_{A,u,v}\in\mathcal P_n\).  By \(\textnormal{ass:exact-rank}\) and \(\textnormal{ass:strong-spectrum}\),
\[
A=USV^{\top},\qquad cn\le s_r(A)\le s_1(A)\le C_0n.
\tag{1}
\]
The span assumptions imply \(u=uVV^{\top}\) and \(v=UU^{\top}v\).  Define
\[
\ell=S^{-1}V^{\top}u^{\top},\qquad q=S^{-1}U^{\top}v,
\qquad
L=\begin{bmatrix}U\\ \ell^{\top}\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
H=\begin{bmatrix}V\\ q^{\top}\end{bmatrix}.
\tag{2}
\]
Then, using \(A^+=VS^{-1}U^{\top}\),
\[
LSH^{\top}
=\begin{bmatrix}
USV^{\top}&USq\\
\ell^{\top}SV^{\top}&\ell^{\top}Sq
\end{bmatrix}
=\begin{bmatrix}A&v\\u&uA^+v\end{bmatrix}
=\overline M_n.
\tag{3}
\]
The first \(n\) rows of \(L\) and \(H\) are the full-column-rank matrices \(U\) and \(V\).  Since \(S\) is invertible, (3) proves \(\operatorname{rank}(\overline M_n)=r\).  By \(\textnormal{ass:gaussian-blocks}\), the three observed blocks in this four-block representation are \(X=A+E\), \(C=v+f\), and \(R=u+e\), with mutually independent entrywise \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) errors.  Thus \(N=T=n+1\), \(N_1=T_1=n\), and \(N_2=T_2=1\) in the notation of Yan and Wainwright~\cite{YanWainwright2024}.

We verify their displayed conditions with the normalization used in that paper.  From \(\textnormal{ass:bounded-entries}\) and (1),
\[
\|\ell\|_2\le {\|u\|_2\over s_r(A)}\le {B\over c\sqrt n},
\qquad
\|q\|_2\le {B\over c\sqrt n}.
\tag{4}
\]
An orthonormal basis of \(\operatorname{col}(L)\) has the form
\[
\overline U=L(L^{\top}L)^{-1/2}O_L
\]
for an orthogonal \(O_L\).  If \(\overline U_1\) denotes its first \(n\) rows, then
\[
\overline U_1^{\top}\overline U_1
=O_L^{\top}(I_r+\ell\ell^{\top})^{-1}O_L.
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (4)--(5) imply, uniformly for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
{1\over2}I_r\preceq\overline U_1^{\top}\overline U_1\preceq I_r.
\tag{6}
\]
The same argument gives (6) for the first \(n\) rows \(\overline V_1\) of an orthonormal basis of \(\operatorname{col}(H)\).  Since \(n/(n+1)\in[1/2,1]\), (6) verifies Yan--Wainwright condition \(4.1\), for example with fixed constants \(c_{\ell}=1/2\) and \(c_u=2\).  Their accompanying size requirement also holds, because \(n\ge c_{\mathrm{size}}\log(2n+2)\) eventually for every fixed \(c_{\mathrm{size}}>0\).

Taking a submatrix cannot increase an ordered singular value.  Since \(A\) is the leading \(n\)-by-\(n\) submatrix of the rank-\(r\) matrix \(\overline M_n\), the min--max characterization gives
\[
\sigma_r^{\star}:=s_r(\overline M_n)\ge s_r(A)\ge cn.
\tag{7}
\]
Yan and Wainwright scale each entry-noise variance as \(\omega^2/(NT)\).  Here that variance is \(\sigma^2\), so the correct identification is
\[
\omega=\sigma\sqrt{NT}=\sigma(n+1),
\tag{8}
\]
not \(\omega=\sigma\).  Consequently their global noise functional in condition \(4.2\) satisfies
\[
\rho_{N,T}={\omega\over\sigma_r^{\star}\sqrt{\min\{N_1,T_1\}}}
\le {\sigma(n+1)\over cn^{3/2}}=O(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(r\le r_0\),
\[
\rho_{N,T}\sqrt{r+\log(N+T)}
\le {\sigma(n+1)\sqrt{r_0+\log(2n+2)}\over cn^{3/2}}
\longrightarrow0,
\tag{10}
\]
which verifies condition \(4.3\) for every fixed positive tolerance.  Their separately defined symbol for the entry-noise standard deviation is \(\omega/\sqrt{NT}=\sigma\).  Hence the local noise quantities in condition \(4.4\) are, correctly,
\[
\rho_N={\sigma\over\sigma_r^{\star}\sqrt{N_1}}
\le {\sigma\over cn^{3/2}},
\qquad
\rho_T\le {\sigma\over cn^{3/2}}.
\tag{11}
\]
Thus (9), rather than (11), is the \(O(n^{-1/2})\) quantity affected by the normalization (8).

The last-row norms of \(\overline U\) and \(\overline V\) are at most \(\|\ell\|_2\) and \(\|q\|_2\).  Therefore the target local-incoherence quantities in condition \(4.4\mathrm a\) obey
\[
\mu_{n+1}=\sqrt{{n+1\over r}}\|\overline U_{n+1,\boldsymbol\cdot}\|_2
\le {\sqrt2B\over c},
\qquad
\nu_{n+1}\le {\sqrt2B\over c}.
\tag{12}
\]
Combining (11)--(12), the first left side in condition \(4.4\mathrm b\) is at most
\[
{\sqrt2B\sigma\sqrt{r_0}\over c^2n^{3/2}}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{13}
\]
and its second left side is at most
\[
{\sqrt2B\sqrt{r_0\log(2n+2)}\over c\sqrt n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{14}
\]
This verifies conditions \(4.4\mathrm a\)--\(4.4\mathrm b\) uniformly.  Conditions \(4.1\)--\(4.4\mathrm b\), including the definition in \(4.2\), therefore hold eventually on this embedded subclass.

Finally, \(u=v=0\) is allowed by the two span assumptions and the entry bound.  Then \(\ell=q=0\), so \(\mu_{n+1}=\nu_{n+1}=0\), whereas \(\rho_N,\rho_T>0\).  The left side of condition \(4.4\mathrm c\) contains
\[
\min\left\{{\rho_T\over\mu_{n+1}},{\rho_N\over\nu_{n+1}}\right\}=+\infty
\tag{15}
\]
under the extended-real convention.  Hence that condition fails at joint zero.  This proves the canonical-subclass claim and does not identify \(\mathcal P_n\) with the full Yan--Wainwright class.

We prove the proposed, operation-count-honest statement.  The elementary enclosure rules follow directly from identities.  If \(\|x-\widehat x\|\le r(x)\) and \(\|y-\widehat y\|\le r(y)\), then
\[
xy-\widehat x\widehat y
=\widehat x(y-\widehat y)+(x-\widehat x)\widehat y
+(x-\widehat x)(y-\widehat y),
\tag{1}
\]
so submultiplicativity gives the stated product radius; addition is the triangle inequality.  Correct directed rounding with a \(q_n\)-bit significand contributes at most \(2^{e_j-q_n}\) when the exact scalar result has magnitude at most \(2^{e_j}\).  Summing these nonnegative radii and applying \(\|M\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|M\|_{\mathrm F}\) transports them to the stated matrix norm.  The mean-value theorem proves the scalar-function rule.

For a candidate inverse \(L\), put \(R=I-KL\).  The input enclosure gives
\[
\|R\|\le\|I-\widehat K L\|+r(K)\|L\|=\varrho(K,L)<1.
\tag{2}
\]
The finite geometric identity and \(\|R^m\|\to0\) imply
\[
(I-R)^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}R^j,
\qquad
\|(I-R)^{-1}-I\|\le{\|R\|\over1-\|R\|}.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(KL=I-R\), equations (2)--(3) yield
\[
\|K^{-1}-L\|
\le{\|L\|\varrho(K,L)\over1-\varrho(K,L)},
\tag{4}
\]
which proves the residual-inverse enclosure.  The addition rule applied to \((S+S^{-1})/2\) proves the local matrix-sign enclosure.  Quantile bisection retains a bracket because it discards a half-interval only when the directed distribution-function enclosure lies strictly on one side of the target probability.  A gate is selected only after its full enclosure separates the threshold; taking the hull otherwise contains every feasible branch.  Induction over the computation graph therefore proves deterministic containment.

We now give the quantitative argument omitted by a bare appeal to polynomially many operations.  Let
\[
H=n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q_n+1\ge2,
\qquad
\varepsilon_0=2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n}.
\tag{5}
\]
Below \(d_0,d_1,\ldots\) are fixed integers, and \(C,C_1,C_2,\ldots\) are finite constants depending only on the declared class constants \(c,C_0,B,\sigma,r_0\); enlarging them finitely does not change their status.  If all current center magnitudes are at most \(H^d\), a matrix multiplication uses at most \(n^3\le H^3\) scalar multiply-adds, every scalar rounding radius is at most \(H^d2^{-q_n}\), and conversion from entrywise radii to Frobenius norm costs at most a factor \(n\le H\).  Thus one such node contributes at most
\[
C H^{d+4}2^{-q_n}.
\tag{6}
\]
The identical count for additions, norms, and scalar nodes is smaller.  Formula (6), rather than an unquantified operation-count assertion, is the transported rounding bound used below.

We next construct every inverse candidate.  Suppose a symmetrized center \(\widehat K\) has certified singular bounds
\[
0<\lambda\le s_{\min}(\widehat K),
\qquad \|\widehat K\|\le\Lambda,
\qquad \lambda^{-1}+\Lambda\le H^{d_0}.
\tag{7}
\]
Starting at \(L_0=\widehat K/\Lambda^2\), perform directed Newton--Schulz steps
\[
L_{k+1}=L_k(2I-\widehat K L_k).
\tag{8}
\]
For an exact step the residual \(R_k=I-\widehat K L_k\) satisfies \(R_{k+1}=R_k^2\).  With directed rounding, (6) gives
\[
r_{k+1}\le r_k^2+\nu,
\qquad
r_k:=\|I-\widehat K L_k\|,
\qquad
\nu=C_1H^{d_1}2^{-q_n},
\tag{9}
\]
and spectral symmetry gives \(1-r_0\ge\lambda^2/\Lambda^2\ge H^{-d_2}\).  Assume first \(\nu\le H^{-2d_2}/8\).  While \(r_k\ge1/2\), equation (9) implies
\[
1-r_{k+1}
\ge(1-r_k)(1+r_k)-\nu
\ge {5\over4}(1-r_k),
\tag{10}
\]
after increasing the fixed large-
\(n\) cutoff.  Hence at most \(\lceil\log_{5/4}(2H^{d_2})\rceil\) steps bring the residual below \(1/2\).  Thereafter, as long as \(r_k\ge2\sqrt\nu\),
\[
r_{k+1}\le {5\over4}r_k^2.
\tag{11}
\]
Thus \((5r_k/4)\) is squared at every such step, and another \(O(\log(q_n+2)+\log\log H)\) steps bring \(r_k\) below \(2\sqrt\nu\); one further step makes it at most \(5\nu\), and (9) then keeps it below \(6\nu\).  Moreover \(\widehat K L_k=I-R_k\), so
\[
\|L_k\|\le\|\widehat K^{-1}\|(1+r_k)\le2H^{d_0}.
\tag{12}
\]
Equations (6), (9)--(12) prove simultaneously that all candidate magnitudes are polynomial, their construction uses the asserted number of \(O(n^3)\) operations, and the directed residual at acceptance is \(O(H^{d_3}2^{-q_n})\).  If an input enclosure for \(K\) has radius \(R_K\), (4) then gives
\[
r(K^{-1})\le C_2H^{d_4}(R_K+2^{1-q_n})
\tag{13}
\]
whenever the right side is below a fixed constant.  If the smallness premise for (10) fails, \(H^{2d_2+d_1}2^{-q_n}\) is bounded below by a fixed constant; increasing the final polynomial exponent makes the coarse-hull bound dominate.  This proves the inverse-candidate claim in both regimes.

We apply (13) first to the matrix-sign computation.  Put \(\tau=(cn/2)^2\).  On the stable box, every eigenvalue of \(X'^{\top}X'-\tau I\) and \(X'X'^{\top}-\tau I\) has absolute value at least
\[
\min\{(3cn/4)^2-(cn/2)^2,(cn/2)^2-(cn/4)^2\}
={3c^2n^2\over16}.
\tag{14}
\]
Their norms are at most \(C n^2\).  Division by a certified power of two between this upper bound and twice it therefore puts every spectrum in
\[
[-1,-\gamma]\cup[\gamma,1]
\tag{15}
\]
for a fixed \(\gamma>0\).  For the exact scalar sign iteration \(x^+=(x+x^{-1})/2\), if \(s=\operatorname{sign}(x)\) and \(z=(x-s)/(x+s)\), direct substitution gives
\[
{x^+-s\over x^++s}=z^2.
\tag{16}
\]
Functional calculus for the symmetric matrices in (15) yields, after \(J\) exact iterations,
\[
\|S_J-\operatorname{sign}(S_0)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le {2\chi^{2^J}\over1-\chi^{2^J}},
\qquad \chi={1-\gamma\over1+\gamma}<1.
\tag{17}
\]
Therefore the radius of \((I\pm S_J)/2\) must, and by construction does, include the exact tail \(\chi^{2^J}/(1-\chi^{2^J})\).

It remains to control noncommutative perturbations of the rounded iterates.  For \(F(S)=(S+S^{-1})/2\), differentiation of \((S+tE)^{-1}(S+tE)=I\) at zero gives
\[
\mathrm DF_S(E)={1\over2}(E-S^{-1}ES^{-1}).
\tag{18}
\]
Equivalently, the resolvent expansion gives
\[
F(S+E)-F(S)=\mathrm DF_S(E)
+{1\over2}S^{-1}ES^{-1}E(S+E)^{-1}.
\tag{19}
\]
After the first exact sign step, every eigenvalue has absolute value at least one.  If the current enclosure radius is at most \(1/4\), (13), (18)--(19), and \(\|S^{-1}\|\le1\), \(\|(S+E)^{-1}\|\le4/3\) give the explicit rounded-iterate recurrence
\[
R_{j+1}\le {3\over2}R_j+C_3H^{d_5}2^{1-q_n}.
\tag{20}
\]
The first step has the same form with a fixed coefficient depending on \(\gamma\).  Solving (20),
\[
R_j\le C_4\left({3\over2}\right)^j
\{R_0+H^{d_5}2^{1-q_n}\}.
\tag{21}
\]
The input-box and Gram-product rules give \(R_0\le C_5H^{d_6}\varepsilon_0\).  Choose
\[
J=\left\lceil
\log_2\left({q_n+d_7\log_2H+2\over|\log_2\chi|}\right)
\right\rceil.
\tag{22}
\]
Then (17) is at most \(H^{-d_7}2^{-q_n}\), while \((3/2)^J\le(H+p_n+q_n)^{d_8}\).  Substitution into (21), together with the exact tail, proves
\[
r(P_L)+r(P_R)
\le C_6H^{d_9}\varepsilon_0.
\tag{23}
\]
Equations (12), (20)--(23) also show that all sign centers, inverses, residuals, and transported rounding radii remain polynomial through the \(O(\log\{q_n+\log H\})\) stages.  This is the requested solved recurrence; it permits noncommuting errors and does not use individual singular vectors.

For the retained pseudoinverse use
\[
X_r=P_LXP_R,
\qquad
K=X_rX_r^{\top}+I-P_L,
\qquad
X_r^+=X_r^{\top}K^{-1}.
\tag{24}
\]
On the exact stable branch, \(K\) has eigenvalue one off the retained space and retained eigenvalues in \([(3cn/4)^2,(3C_0n/2)^2]\).  Thus (7) holds with \(\lambda\ge1/2\) after allowing for (23), and \(\Lambda\le H^{d_{10}}\).  The explicit residual-squaring construction (8)--(13), followed by the product rule, proves
\[
r(X_r^+)\le C_7H^{d_{11}}\varepsilon_0.
\tag{25}
\]
Repeated positive singular values cause no difficulty because (17), (23)--(25) concern invariant projectors and the full pseudoinverse.  A tie across the retained--discarded split is never accepted.

Finally, on the stable branch \(\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\asymp n^{-1}\), while the encoded observations are bounded by \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\).  Every product, norm, and argument of \(\log\) or the localized square root in the analytic endpoint is therefore bounded by a power of \(H\); logarithm arguments are at least one, and the square-root argument in \(R_{0,n}\) is bounded away from zero.  Norms and maxima are enclosed by their one-Lipschitz interval rules, including at zero.  The tail probabilities entering the normal and fixed-degree chi-square quantiles are bounded below by \(\alpha/(4H^{d_{12}})\).  The Gaussian identity \(-\phi'(x)=x\phi(x)\) and the even-degree formula
\[
1-F_{\chi^2_{2r}}(x)=e^{-x/2}\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}{(x/2)^j\over j!}
\tag{26}
\]
show that the reciprocal densities at the relevant quantiles are at most a power of \(H\).  Hence probability-bracketed bisection and every remaining scalar recurrence multiply (23)--(25) by only a fixed power of \(H\).  There are at most a polynomial number of such scalar operations, so the explicit count (6) gives
\[
r(\hbox{every final node})\le K_\star H^{k_\star}\varepsilon_0.
\tag{27}
\]
If the right side is not small enough to certify the branch, the coarse hull has radius at most another fixed power of \(H\); choosing \(k_\star\) larger makes (27) dominate because failure of the smallness condition supplies the reciprocal power of \(H\).  This proves the quantitative and complexity clauses.  Giving a control interval half its width as initial radius preserves the enclosure induction, but (6)--(27) cannot bound the cost of generating that interval without a uniform modulus, proving the last clause.

On \(\kappa_n=0\), every point of \(\mathcal B_n\) has coordinate magnitude at most \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1\).  On a feasible on-gate branch,
\[
\|X_r^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le{2\over cn},
\qquad
\|Z_{p,n}\|_2\vee\|Z_{q,n}\|_2
\le{\sqrt n(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)\over\sigma},
\qquad
t_{Z,n}\le{\sqrt{2n}(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)\over\sigma}.
\tag{1}
\]
It follows directly from \(\textnormal{def:analytic-halfwidth}\), using \(\log(e+x)\le1+x\) and \(\sqrt x\le1+x\), that the center and analytic half-width are bounded by a fixed power of
\[
H_n=n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q_n+1.
\tag{2}
\]
The donor allowance has the same property by \(\textnormal{def:donor-allowance}\), and the off-gate radius \(M_0=B^2/c\) is fixed.  The outward hull of these branches therefore has radius at most \(K H_n^k\).  The certificate may use this hull whenever a sharp decision is unavailable, proving the first bound.

Now impose the three stable spectral inequalities.  With \(\tau=(cn/2)^2\), the distance of every squared singular value from \(\tau\) is at least
\[
\min\{(3cn/4)^2-(cn/2)^2,(cn/2)^2-(cn/4)^2\}
={3c^2n^2\over16}.
\tag{3}
\]
The proposed and proved quantitative clause of \(\textnormal{lem:certified-error-recurrence}\) applies to (3).  In particular, its explicit residual-squaring construction certifies every inverse, its noncommutative recurrence controls the rounded sign iterates, and its projector radius includes the exact truncation tail
\[
{\chi^{2^J}\over1-\chi^{2^J}}.
\tag{4}
\]
That lemma gives, for each endpoint node and every radius transported into it,
\[
r\le K H_n^k(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n}).
\tag{5}
\]
The lower bound on \(s_r(X')\) justifies the retained inverse, the bound on \(s_{r+1}(X')\) certifies the split, and the largest-singular-value bound controls all intermediate magnitudes.  Because only invariant projectors occur, repeated retained singular values are allowed.  Exact-dyadic controls have zero initial radius.

By \(\textnormal{def:numerical-padding}\), \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) and \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\) are sums of the nonnegative radii transported through this finite computation graph.  The number of scalar operations, inverse residual-squaring steps, sign steps, and bisection steps is at most a fixed power of \(H_n\), as counted explicitly in the recurrence proof.  Increasing \(K_\star,k_\star\) in (5) therefore bounds their sum by the second displayed inequality in the proposed statement.  Each recorded summand is nonnegative and no larger than that sum.  This proves every assertion.

theorem.statement:
For exact-dyadic public controls, the certified-implementation question has an affirmative answer with
\[
h_\alpha=\lceil\log_2(64/\alpha)\rceil,
\quad g_n=20\{h_\alpha+\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil+1\},
\quad p_n=n^2+4g_n,
\quad q_n=p_n-g_n,
\]
\[
\tau_n=B+\sigma\sqrt{12\log(e+n)}+1,
\quad
\overline\tau_n=B+\sigma\{12(n+1)+1\}+1,
\quad
L_n=p_n+\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil
+\lceil\log_2\overline\tau_n\rceil+2g_n+C_\star
\]
for a sufficiently large fixed \(C_\star\).  These schedules give \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\ge\tau_n\), uniform asymptotic \((1-\alpha)\)-coverage, \(P(\kappa_n=1)=o(n^{-1})\), \(\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]/w_n\to0\), transition-order expected length, and the oracle Gaussian length along every sequence with \(b_n/a_n\to0\).  Every recorded numerical-radius summand and the fallback contribution have expectation \(o(n^{-1})\), uniformly over \(\mathcal P_n\), including rank-one joint zero.  On \(\kappa_n=0\), \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\) and \(0\le\varepsilon_n\le2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}}\); on \(\kappa_n=1\), the output is \([-M_0,M_0]\).  For a non-dyadic refinable control, the same polynomial-time conclusion requires an explicit uniform time-and-output-size modulus incorporated into the schedules; one fixed nonrefinable interval is insufficient.
theorem.proof_tex: This is the exact-dyadic specialization of the proved, corrected \(\textnormal{thm:certified-implementation}\).  Its displayed schedules, containment, coverage, expectation, transition-length, oracle-length, and rank-one joint-zero conclusions are identical.  The last sentence follows from the indistinguishability argument in the final paragraph of that theorem's proof.

For every execution of \(H_n^{\mathrm{cert}}\), attach to each scalar, vector, or matrix node \(x\) a computed center \(\widehat x\) and a nonnegative outward radius \(r(x)\) in the norm specified for that node. Whenever the right side is below a fixed class-dependent constant, the sharp spectral branch is certified; otherwise the valid coarse hull is returned, and, after increasing \(K_\star,k_\star\), it obeys the same displayed bound. \[
h_\alpha=\lceil\log_2(64/\alpha)\rceil,
\qquad
g_n=20\{h_\alpha+\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil+1\},
\]
\[
p_n=n^2+4g_n,\qquad q_n=p_n-g_n,\qquad
\tau_n=B+\sigma\sqrt{12\log(e+n)}+1,
\]
and define the exactly comparable dyadic upper bound
\[
\overline\tau_n=B+\sigma\{12(n+1)+1\}+1\ge\tau_n.
\]
For a sufficiently large fixed integer \(C_\star\), put
\[
L_n=p_n+\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil
+\lceil\log_2\overline\tau_n\rceil+2g_n+C_\star.
\]
Then these schedules are polynomially bounded in \(n\) and \(\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\), \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\ge\tau_n\), and the composed measurable interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\) satisfies
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\}\ge1-\alpha,
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(\kappa_n=1)=o(n^{-1}),
\]
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}{\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]\over w_n}\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
{\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})]\over w_n}
\le K_\alpha.
\]
On \(\kappa_n=0\),
\[
I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}},
\qquad
0\le\varepsilon_n\le2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}};
\]
on \(\kappa_n=1\), \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}=[-M_0,M_0]\).  Along every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(b_n/a_n\to0\),
\[
{\varepsilon_n\over a_n}\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in \(L^1(P_n)\) and in probability},
\qquad
{\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})
\over2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\]
Finally, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the expectation of every nonnegative recorded summand of \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) and \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), the fallback contribution \(M_0\mathbf1\{\kappa_n=1\}\), and \(\varepsilon_n\) is \(o(n^{-1})\).  In particular, this holds along every sequence with \(r=1\) and \(u=v=0\).  A polynomial-time extension to refinable non-dyadic controls requires schedules parameterized by an explicit uniform time-and-output-size modulus.

prose_updates.tldr: A strong donor block identifies the missing untreated panel mean as \(\theta_n=uA^+v\), but a purely Gaussian first-order interval is not uniformly valid when target loadings vanish. The donor-only analytic interval retains the bilinear term through an exact conditional Gaussian reduction, covers uniformly over the known-rank strong-donor class, has expected length of order \(w_n=a_n+b_n\), recovers the Gaussian oracle constant along every first-order-dominant sequence, and matches the transition order through an interior local Kullback--Leibler lower bound. A measurable finite-range dyadic encoding followed by the certified outward algorithm now preserves these guarantees: every numerical padding component is uniformly \(o(n^{-1})\), including at rank-one joint zero. The polynomial-time headline uses exact-dyadic public controls; refinable non-dyadic controls require an explicit uniform refinement modulus.

project_justification.fill: The project derives the donor-conditional Gaussian experiment, constructs an analytic outer interval with an observable donor allowance and bounded fallback, proves transition-order upper and local lower length results together with every-sequence oracle length, and closes the implementation transfer with explicit encoding schedules, residual-certified Newton--Schulz inverses, a noncommutative rounded matrix-sign recurrence with exact truncation tails, probability-bracketed quantiles, and an uncertain-gate hull. The finite-precision theorem applies to continuous Gaussian observations after measurable encoding and to exact-dyadic public controls; the subclass lower bound transfers upward to every containing model class.

prose_updates.related_work: Yan and Wainwright (2024) supply the four-block spectral estimator, its master expansion, regular Gaussian interval, and lower-bound architecture. Under their normalization \(\omega=\sigma\sqrt{NT}\), the present model is a canonical square one-target subclass with \(\rho_{N,T}=O(n^{-1/2})\); their Gaussian theorem still requires condition \(4.4\mathrm c\), which fails at joint-zero loadings. The upper comparison is only on this embedded subclass, while the proved local lower bound on the subclass transfers upward to every model class containing it. Bei and Navjeevan (2026) provide the general first-order-degeneracy inference context, while the narrow contribution here is the complete strong-donor panel transfer and all-sequence length theorem. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright (2025) and CAST are the direct consumer. Existing verified-SVD and floating-point work informs the arithmetic design, but the proof here supplies the missing coupled certificate for invariant projectors, pseudoinverses, quantiles, gate uncertainty, and measurable observation encoding. The polynomial-time statement is intentionally limited to exact-dyadic public controls unless a uniform refinement modulus is supplied.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The certificate is a mathematical bit-model theorem for MPFR-equivalent directed radix-two arithmetic, not a verification of a particular software implementation. Its sharp branch uses invariant spectral projectors and therefore permits repeated retained singular values, but it falls back to a bounded outward hull when the retained--discarded split or gate cannot be certified. Public controls are exact dyadics in the headline theorem; an arbitrary fixed enclosing interval is insufficient for shrinking quantile enclosures, and a refinable non-dyadic control needs an explicit uniform time-and-output-size modulus. The statistical model still assumes known rank and variance, independent Gaussian blocks, strong donors, and exact span membership.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The result covers continuously distributed Gaussian observations in square known-rank strong-donor panels after a measurable finite-range dyadic encoding. It proves uniform coverage, transition-order expected length, every-sequence oracle Gaussian length, and uniformly negligible certified numerical padding, including rank-one joint zero. It does not claim unknown-rank adaptation, approximate-factor or weak-donor robustness, dependent or unknown-variance inference, a verified production implementation, or inference for a realized untreated outcome. The Yan--Wainwright comparison is only on the canonical embedded square one-target subclass, never their full published class. Polynomial bit complexity assumes exact-dyadic public controls; a non-dyadic refinement oracle must carry a uniform modulus into the schedules.
